newsitem.title: UK: Copenhagen Re pools assets to improve security.
newsitem.headline: Copenhagen Re pools assets to improve security.

text.p: Danish reinsurance group Copenhagen Re is centralising the assets of its subsidiaries in response to growing emphasis on financial security in the market, the group said on Monday.

Copenhagen Re plans to turn its London and Singapore subsidiaries into branches of its Danish parent. At the same time all insurance assets and liabilities of the subsidiaries will be transferred to the branches and controlled from head office.

"The reasons for this decision are the advantages to the market of offering our clients the full security of the parent company as well as the expertise of the entire group," a company statement said.
Group managing director Leif Corinth-Hansen said: "This is an example of a successful company moving with the times. All our operations have made consistently good profits in the past three years.
"By improving our security we will be able to see more business and use our assets more efficiently."
Copenhagen Re Group, part of Denmark's Alm. Brand Group, has shareholder funds of 1.51 billion crowns ($228 million) and total equity including equalisation reserves of 1.81 billion crowns.
Gross premium income in 1997 is expected to exceed 2.2 billion crowns originating from world markets, the statement said.
The newly-created branches, subject to regulatory approval, will continue with business as usual alongside another branch in Australia and a representative office in Chile.
-- Gordon Mackenzie Reuters Insurance News +44 171 542 2770 ($ = 6.622 Danish Crowns)
